sections.title: Crypto Exchange Metrics
sections.subtitle: Trading volume, revenue mix and the metric management guides to

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Coinbase Global, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Coinbase Global, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Coinbase: this is GAAP EBITDA, not the Adjusted EBITDA figure management guides to (see the Adjusted EBITDA chart) -- it still carries crypto asset gains/losses and other GAAP items that swing with the market.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

tradingVolume.title: Trading volume
tradingVolume.content:
Trading volume is the total dollar value of crypto bought and sold on Coinbase's platform in the period, across retail (consumer) and institutional (prime) order flow.

For Coinbase: this is the single biggest swing factor in the model -- transaction revenue is a take rate applied to volume, and volume itself tracks crypto market prices and volatility far more than any secular growth trend. Quarters with a crypto rally or crash can move volume 2-3x in either direction.

What to watch:

  • Volume falling even as crypto prices rise (market-share loss to on-chain/DEX trading)
  • The mix shift toward institutional volume, which carries a much lower take rate
  • Log scale is on by default given the multi-year range

revenueMix.title: Revenue mix: transaction vs subscription & services
revenueMix.content:
Transaction revenue is trading fees -- volume x take rate, and the most volatile line. Subscription & services revenue (custody, staking, Coinbase One, USDC/stablecoin interest, blockchain rewards) is largely volume-independent and recurs quarter to quarter.

For Coinbase: management's whole growth narrative is this mix shifting toward subscription revenue so earnings don't collapse every time crypto prices fall. The line on the right axis is the share of total revenue subscription now represents.

What to watch:

  • Subscription share rising through a down-crypto quarter (the thesis working)
  • Transaction revenue still dwarfing subscription in a bull run (take-rate compression risk if it doesn't)

adjustedEbitda.title: Adjusted EBITDA
adjustedEbitda.content:
Adjusted EBITDA is Coinbase's own non-GAAP metric: GAAP EBITDA adjusted to strip out stock-based comp, crypto asset gains/losses, and other items management considers non-operating. It is the single figure Coinbase highlights in every earnings release and the metric guidance is framed against.

For Coinbase: the gap between Adjusted and GAAP EBITDA is mostly stock-based comp -- a real dilution cost the DCF charges back even though Adjusted EBITDA excludes it.

What to watch:

  • Adjusted EBITDA margin holding up through a volume downturn (the subscription-revenue thesis)
  • How wide the Adjusted-vs-GAAP gap is running, and whether SBC is growing as a share of it

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Coinbase Global, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Coinbase Global, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Coinbase Global, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Coinbase Global, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Coinbase Global, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Coinbase Global, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Coinbase Global, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
